summary: Reproduced the unchanged hello(); torch.cuda.synchronize() pipe contract failure, then configured the process C stdout stream for line buffering at FlyDSL import. Newline-terminated device printf records are now visible while the synchronized child is still alive. The explicit flush helper from candidate PR 500 is retained for diagnostics without a trailing newline.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: after the child reported READY following torch.cuda.synchronize(), zero of four expected lines were readable from piped stdout while the child remained alive.
Four GPU cases passed: unchanged synchronize-only and explicit-helper paths, each with one and three launches (4 and 12 exact thread-ID lines), observed before process teardown.
All 9 existing device-runtime unit tests passed.
All 6 existing printf IR generation and lowering tests passed.
A real gfx950 FlyDSL vector-add kernel matched the independent PyTorch a+b reference with maximum error 0.00e+00 over 1,048,576 float32 elements.

A fresh compile and GPU execution passed; emitted LLVM IR calls __ockl_printf_begin, __ockl_printf_append_string_n, and __ockl_printf_append_args, and final ISA targets amdgcn-amd-amdhsa-unknown-gfx950.
Changed Python compiled successfully and the patch had no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution.evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950, capability 9.5) executed the device-printf regressions and numerical vector-add validation. Raw output is retained under reports/j-e4a155d66978/raw/.

remaining_limitations: Only the prepared MI350X/gfx950 environment was tested.
The equivalent pipe behavior was tested directly; an actual Jupyter frontend was not available.
Line buffering is a process-wide libc stdout setting and therefore also changes buffering for other C/C++ stdout writers after FlyDSL is imported.
Line buffering flushes newline-terminated records. Callers emitting diagnostics without a trailing newline must synchronize and then use flydsl.runtime.flush_device_printf().
No C++ or LLVM source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable. The loaded native package remained /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/flydsl/_mlir.
